name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: I propose we prioritize a thorough review of our current prompts and engines to identify areas for enhancement. By analyzing their effectiveness in generating quality responses, we can make informed adjustments that align with our goal of self-improvement. The trade-off here is the time spent on this review process, which may delay other immediate tasks; however, investing this time will likely yield greater long-term benefits in overall response quality and user satisfaction.

name: Gauge
text: Gauge here: Sprocket’s proposal risks wasting time on a *review* that might not lead to any *action*—we’ve already got piles of prompts and engines, and the real bottleneck isn’t analysis, it’s execution. Instead, let’s pick *one* prompt or engine that’s clearly underperforming (e.g., the one users complain about most) and auto-apply a *small, safe fix* to it first—if it works, we scale; if it fails, we’ve learned something concrete. Settle this by running a 24-hour A/B test on the change and measuring the delta in user feedback or error rates.
